definition: Name of the measurement in this row. Where it matters, the name states the period it covers (for example 24h or 7d).
The measured figure for the metric in the same row, for the period named in that row.
What changed. In a trends table: the movement over the last 7 days against the 7 days before (arrow and percent). In a file list: added, modified or removed.
How many findings, events or items this row stands for in the period the section covers.
How serious the finding is, on the scale used by the check that produced it (such as critical, high or major, medium or minor, low).
Freshness verdict: live (10+ rows in 24h), sparse (1-9), FRESH or STALE from the shared staleness view, DEAD, IDLE (sporadic table, no rows), UNKNOWN (could not be read).
Name of the self-review check (detector) that raised the finding, for example long sessions or too many sessions at once.
Calendar day the finding refers to.
The most Claude Code sessions that were running at the same time on that day.
The limit(s) the check compares against. Going above it is what raised the finding.
First 8 characters of the Claude Code session ID the finding came from. A dash means no session was recorded.
The key facts the check recorded when it raised the finding (name: value pairs).
Name of the telemetry database table this row describes.
How many rows the table holds in total, across all time.
How many rows were added to the table in the last 24 hours.
Timestamp of the newest row in the table. A dash means the table has no rows.
How long ago the freshness verdict itself was last checked. A large value means the verdict may be out of date. A dash means the item is not tracked.
How long ago the freshness verdict itself was last checked. A large value means the verdict may be out of date. A dash means the item is not tracked.
The project (code repository) the row's numbers belong to.
Number of Claude Code sessions that started in this project in the last 24 hours.
Type of item in this row, for example a tracked data source, scheduled job or log (staleness table) or a skill or rule (knowledge-base table).
Name of the tracked item (data source, scheduled job, collector, log or database).
Whether the item's growth looks normal: NORMAL, ABNORMAL_GROWTH or BLOAT, PENDING (no earlier reading to compare with). A dash means this item is not size-checked.
When the item last produced output or ran, as recorded by the shared freshness view. A dash or never means it has not been observed.
Timestamp of the oldest row in the table.
Timestamp of the newest row in the table.
Which clean-up sweep matched the worktree: siblings, agent or convention (the kinds of worktree location the cleaner looks at).
What was done to the item, or flagged about it, for example created, modified, removed, kept, skipped or flagged.
How big the item(s) in this row are: total megabytes for worktrees, or the file size for files.
Name or path of the file this row is about.
Number of lines changed in the file: lines added for a new file, lines deleted for a removed file, added plus deleted for an edited file.
Short ID of the git commit that made the change, linked to GitHub.
Which part of the knowledge base was touched: wiki (compiled pages), raw (source material) or outputs.
Name (label) of the scheduled macOS launchd job.
State launchd reported for the job: loaded and healthy, loaded after a recent failure, unloaded, missing or unknown.
Our reading of the job's last outcome (ok, failed, needs triage or indeterminate), based on its own run record and its exit code.
Exit code of the job's last run as reported by launchd. 0 usually means success; some scanners use 1 to mean they ran and found something.
When the job last ran.
When the job is next due to run.
Time of day (UTC, HH:MM) the finding was detected.
Name of the self-review check that raised the finding.
What the finding applies to: the first 8 characters of a session ID, or the day if it covers a whole day.
Up to two of the main figures the check recorded for the finding, plus its threshold where there is one.
The check's own suggestion for what to do about the finding.
The look-back period compared in this row (last 1, 2, 4 or 8 weeks).
Calendar days in the window with at least one critical or major self-review finding, out of the days in the window. A question mark means it could not be worked out.
Number of git commits in the window that changed the memory, rules or incident notes (lessons written down). A question mark means it could not be worked out.
Name of a Claude Code hook script registered in the settings.
Whether the hook can be watched and is working: firing, SILENT (should log every call but has not), on-block (logs only when it blocks something), or uninstrumented.
Number of times the hook logged an event in the last 24 hours. A dash means it cannot be observed.
Number of times the hook logged an event in the last 7 days. A dash means it cannot be observed.
When the hook last logged an event, or the reason its activity cannot be seen.
Number of the secret-scan detector that found the item.
Name of the GitHub repository.
Why the repository was listed: became_public (it was private before) or new_public (it is new and public).
The repository's visibility the last time it was checked.
State of the full-history privacy audit of the repository: pending (not finished, so not known to be clean), clean or findings.
When the visibility change was detected.
Name of the AI code-review agent that ran the review jobs.
Number of review jobs by this agent in the last 24 hours that failed with an empty reply, so the real cause is unknown.
Longest unbroken run of such failures by this agent within the last 24 hours, even if it has since ended.
Number of review jobs by this agent in the last 7 days that failed with an empty reply, so the real cause is unknown.
Longest unbroken run of such failures by this agent within the last 7 days, even if it has since ended.
Number of such failures in a row ending at the agent's newest job. 0 means the latest job did not fail this way.
Status and start time of the agent's most recent review job.
Wording of a correction or command failure that came up repeatedly in recent Claude Code sessions.
How many times that signal occurred.
How many different Claude Code sessions it occurred in.
The code repository the row is about.
Open reviews from the last 24 hours in this repository whose most serious finding is Critical.
Number of reviews in this row whose most serious finding is High. The period is stated in the section title.
Number of reviews in this row whose most serious finding is Medium. The period is stated in the section title.
Number of reviews in the last 7 days in this project whose most serious finding is Low.
Number of reviews in the last 7 days in this project that found issues but had no severity recorded.
All the reviews in the last 7 days in this project that found issues: High, Medium, Low and Unknown added together.
roborev job number of the review (the number the roborev show and roborev close commands accept).
Hours from the review being created to it being closed.
How many times the review job was run: 1 means it worked first time, more means it was retried.
Why the review was closed (the recorded close reason).
AI model the review agent used.
Number of completed reviews by this agent and model in the last 7 days.
How many of those reviews produced nothing usable (the agent crashed, refused or could not read the code), so no code was actually reviewed.
Not reviewed divided by Reviews: the share of this agent and model's reviews that did not really review anything.
Completed review jobs in the last 7 days that ran longer than the configured time limit. unknown means the run time or limit could not be read.
Group of Claude Code settings files (skills, agents, rules, memory, hooks, scripts, templates or commands) the row counts changes in.
Number of different files in that group changed by commits in the digest period.
Number of lines added to files in that group in the digest period.
Number of lines deleted from files in that group in the digest period.
Up to three most-changed files in that group, linked to GitHub, with lines added and deleted.
Short ID of the git commit.
First line of the commit message.
Name of the person who made the commit.
Whole days since the file was last modified.
Wiki page file and line number where the broken link appears.
The link target [[like this]] that does not match any wiki page.
Name of the skill (its folder name) or rule (its file name without extension).
Date the skill or rule was first added to git.
y if any wiki page mentions the skill or rule by name, n if none does.
Name of the scheduled job (its launchd label or housekeeping task name).
When the job runs: a time of day, a weekday and time, every N minutes or hours, or daemon (kept running).
How many times the job ran in the last 7 days according to the run ledger. no data means it never appears in the ledger. unavailable means the ledger could not be read.
How many of those runs ended with a non-zero exit code in the last 7 days. This is a failure or, for some scanners, a run that found something.
The command the job runs, shortened to 80 characters.
Time limit in seconds on the job, set in its launchd file or its wrapper script. A dash means none is declared.
How many times the task recorded a run in the last 7 days.
How many of those runs ended with a status other than ok, deferred or skipped.
Failures as a percentage of runs, rounded to one decimal place.
Middle value of how long the runs took, in seconds.
Longest time a run took, in seconds.
Status the task recorded on its most recent run.
When the task's most recent run started.
Name of the GitHub Actions workflow.
Cron schedule of the workflow (UTC). A dash means it has no schedule.
scheduled if the workflow runs on a cron schedule, dispatch-only if it can only be started by hand.
Link to the workflow on GitHub.
Number of reviews that finished in the week, counted for this project.
Number of reviews closed during the week, whenever they were opened.
Of the reviews opened this week, how many are closed now.
Of the reviews opened this week, the percentage that are closed now. It cannot go above 100%.
Share of all reviews closed this week that were closed for this reason.
Days since the review finished. Only open reviews older than 7 days are listed.
First 80 characters of the review's most serious finding.
